newsitem.title: USA: Woolworth names chief financial officer.
newsitem.headline: Woolworth names chief financial officer.

text.p: Woolworth Corp., which is in the midst of shedding its flagship five-and-dime stores, on Wednesday named Reid Johnson chief financial officer.
Johnson's appointment is effective September 8 and fills a post that has been vacant since April.
Johnson comes to Woolworth from Musicland, where he was chief financial officer of the retail music chain. He succeeds Andrew Hines, who resigned to pursue other interests.

Johnson takes over at a time when Woolworth is in the midst of closing 400 of its discount stores, converting about 100 of them to Foot Locker shoe stores, Champs Sports stores or other specialty formats.
The move came as Woolworth struggled to keep pace with new competitors in the discount retail field, including Wal-Mart Stores Inc., Kmart Corp. and Target, a division of Dayton Hudson Corp..

"With Reid's extensive retail background in finance, treasury, information systems, real estate and distribution, he will bring an added dimension and important strength to our management team," Woolworth Chairman and Chief Executive Roger Farah said in a statement.
Woolworth operates more than 7,100 retail stores in 12 countries in North America, Europe and Australia.
